title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. T̂^+_{1,1} ≅ SL(2,Z)^ is the profinite completion of the orientation-preserving mapping class group of the once-punctured torus, i.e. the geometric fundamental group of the stack M_{1,1}. Γ_Q (written Π_Q on the next page) is Gal(Q̄/Q). The arithmetic fundamental group of M_{1,1,Q} is the extension (1): 1 → T̂^+_{1,1} → N_{1,1} → Γ_Q → 1. It induces an outer action Γ_Q → Out(SL(2,Z)^).

The point made on this page. The centre {±1} of SL(2,Z)^ is non-trivial; it is the generic automorphism −1 of every elliptic curve. So the outer action alone does not reconstruct the extension N_{1,1}, even up to unique isomorphism. Extensions with a given outer action are governed by H^2(Γ_Q, centre), and isomorphisms between them are only unique up to H^1(Γ_Q, centre).

What the outer action does give is an extension N'_{1,1} of Γ_Q by the centreless quotient SL(2,Ẑ)' := SL(2,Z)^/{±1} = PSL(2,Z)^. It is obtained by pulling back the canonical extension (13): 1 → G → Aut(G) → Out(G) → 1, with G = SL(2,Ẑ)' centreless, along Γ_Q → Out(G). Geometrically N'_{1,1} is π_1 of the ±1-rigidified moduli stack, i.e. the orbifold j-line.

Alternative interpretation. N'_{1,1} is also the extension M_{0,3} ≅ N'_{0,4} of Γ_Q by Ĝ_{0,3} ≅ T̂'_{0,4}. Here Ĝ_{0,3} is an extension of S_3 ≅ SL(2,Z/2) by π̂_{0,3} = π̂_1(P^1 − {0,1,∞}), which is a free profinite group on 2 generators. This matches the classical facts:
- Γ(2)/{±1} ≅ F_2;
- PSL(2,Z)/Γ̄(2) ≅ S_3;
- the λ-line P^1 − {0,1,∞} with its S_3-action has quotient the j-line;
- equivalently M_{0,4} modulo the Klein four-group.

Known facts recalled:
- The outer action of Γ_Q on π̂_{0,3} is faithful (Belyi).
- It commutes with the outer action of S_3 = SL(2,Ẑ)'/π̂_{0,3}.

Where this leads. The page sets up the next one. There the commutation is reinterpreted as a consequence of a 'congruence' description. Γ_Q acts on the congruence quotients SL(2,Z/n) through the cyclotomic character, χ mod squares, giving (Z/n)^*/(Z/n)^{*2} → Autext(SL(2,Z/n)). For n = 2 this group is trivial. For level 2m it gives subtler congruence relations, to be expressed via the kernels Π(2m) ⊂ π̂_{0,3} of T̂ → SL(2,Z/2m).

Purpose. This is part of an attempt to characterize the image of Γ_Q in Out(π̂_{0,3}), i.e. Grothendieck–Teichmüller-type constraints coming from the modular tower at genus 1 and level structures.
errors: No mathematical error visible. The statements are sketched rather than proved.
Notation is loose: Γ_Q here vs Π_Q on the next page. The middle term of (13) is written ambiguously (Aut_loc/Autext); it should be Aut(SL(2,Ẑ)') → Out(SL(2,Ẑ)').
SL(2,Ẑ)' denotes SL(2,Z)^/{±1}, not a quotient of the congruence completion SL(2,Ẑ). The notation conflates the two, although the 'déf' clarifies the intent.

ideas.what: Non-trivial centre {±1} prevents reconstructing the arithmetic fundamental group extension of M_{1,1} from the outer Galois action; only the extension by the centreless quotient PSL(2,Z)^ is determined (pullback of Aut→Out).
ideas.modern_name: Outer actions vs extensions; rigidification of M_{1,1} by the generic ±1 inertia
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard group cohomology; in the anabelian/GT context Nakamura, Lochak–Nakamura–Schneps (1990s)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses T_{1,1}, SL(2,Z)^ and Γ_Q acting on the Teichmüller tower in general terms

ideas.what: Identification of PSL(2,Z)^ = T̂'_{1,1} with T̂'_{0,4}, an extension of S_3 ≅ SL(2,Z/2) by π̂_1(P^1−{0,1,∞}); the arithmetic extension as π_1 of the λ-line modulo S_3.
ideas.modern_name: Γ(2)/±1 ≅ F_2, j-line as S_3-quotient of the λ-line; M_{1,1} vs M_{0,4}
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical; in Galois/GT context Ihara, Nakamura, Lochak–Schneps
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (genus 0/1 low-dimensional modular stacks, M_{0,4} and M_{1,1})

ideas.what: Faithfulness of the Γ_Q outer action on π̂_{0,3} and its commutation with the S_3 action, reinterpreted as a level-2 case of congruence relations given by the cyclotomic character mod squares acting on SL(2,Z/n).
ideas.modern_name: Galois action on congruence quotients via det/Weil pairing; congruence-type constraints on GT
ideas.usually_credited_to: Belyi (faithfulness); Ihara, Nakamura, Lochak–Nakamura–Schneps (genus-one/SL(2) constraints on GT)

missed.claim: Grothendieck proposes deriving explicit 'congruence relations' on the outer Galois action on π̂_{0,3}. These would come from the level-2m principal congruence kernels Π(2m) ⊂ π̂_{0,3} and the action via (Z/2m)^*/squares. It is a programme for genus-one/congruence constraints on the image of Γ_Q in Out(F̂_2). Related constraints were later developed (Lochak–Nakamura–Schneps, Nakamura, Boggi), so novelty is limited. This specific formulation via χ mod squares on S_3-invariant congruence kernels is not, to my knowledge, explicitly in print under his name.
missed.quote: Mais cette commutation peut maintenant [s'interpréter ... comme un cas très particulier de relations congruentielles nettement plus subtiles]
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It gives a concrete set of congruence conditions that could be compared with the defining relations of ĜT and its genus-one variants. It may yield explicit additional constraints or a historical precursor attribution.

deep.surprise_reason: The page mostly contains routine observations about centres and outer actions and the classical PSL(2,Z)/S_3/F_2 dictionary, in a GT/Galois context Grothendieck already sketched in the Esquisse. The congruence-relations programme is interesting but largely parallels later published work.
transcription_corrections: 'ne provient pas a priori de réconstitution' should read roughly 'ne permet pas a priori de reconstituer (à iso unique près)'.
'Elle donne seulement l'extension N'_{1,1}' is correct; 'extension [-Γ-]' is a struck-out symbol.

In (13) the middle and right terms appear as Aut_{loc}(Sl(2,Ẑ)^') → Autext_{loc}(Sl(2,Ẑ)^'), with several crossed-out attempts, rather than Autext_ext. Read it as 1 → Sl(2,Ẑ)' → Aut(Sl(2,Ẑ)') → Autext(Sl(2,Ẑ)') → 1.
'Γ_Q' is written with a double-struck symbol; it matches 'Π_Q' on the next page.
'groupe qui est lui-même ext de G_3 ≅ Sl(2,Z/2Z)': G_3 is 𝔖_3 (script S), not G.
